transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, it's nice to meet you too. Um, I guess what brings me in is that my sleep has gotten really, really messed up lately. I’ll either stay up half the night with my mind just... running, or I wake up way too early feeling like I never even went to sleep. It’s so frustrating. Actually, it kind of reminds me of when I was working at this accounting firm right out of high school—my boss there was this older guy, Mr. Henderson, and he used to come in at like 4:30 in the morning. He was always drinking this awful-smelling chicory coffee. I could never understand how he functioned. But now, here I am, up at the crack of dawn, except I don't drink chicory coffee. I mostly just drink green tea, though sometimes that gives me heartburn if I drink it on an empty stomach. Anyway, yeah, I just... I can't seem to get a normal night's rest anymore.
Have you had a time when you felt unusually energized or high, beyond your normal self?

Energized? Yeah, um, earlier in the month I actually felt almost... lit up, I guess? Like I was completely unstoppable. I was flying through all my bookkeeping stuff. Which is honestly a miracle because my supervisor, Brenda, she insists on using this ancient version of Excel. I keep telling her she needs to update it, but she won't, and she prints out literally every single invoice. It’s such a massive waste of paper, and the printer always jams on the second floor anyway because it's as old as she is. 

But anyway, yeah, I felt super energized and unstoppable, but then... I don't know, I’d just snap at her. Or at my mom. Like, they’d ask me these tiny, little questions that normally wouldn’t bother me at all, and I'd just bite their heads off. My mom just asked me if I wanted chicken or fish for dinner one night, and I got so mad at her. She always buys that cheap frozen tilapia, and honestly, it just tastes like lake water. I keep telling her to get the fresh stuff from the deli counter, but she clips coupons. But yeah, I guess I did feel really high energy and just... irritable for a bit there.
During that energized stretch, did you feel like you needed less sleep than usual?

Yeah, actually, that's exactly what it was like. There were a few nights where I think I only slept maybe three or four hours, tops. But when I woke up, I didn't even feel tired. I felt completely charged, like I didn't even need coffee. Which is funny, because usually I need at least one cup to even form a sentence. I used to go to this little coffee shop down the street from my apartment, they had this amazing vanilla hazelnut blend. But then they changed management and the new guy, I think his name is Todd, he completely changed the menu. Now it's all these weird, overly complicated lattes with like, lavender and oat milk. I tried one once and it tasted like a candle. I just don't understand why people want to drink things that taste like potpourri. It’s like when people put rosemary in bread—it just tastes like pine needles. But anyway, yeah, I didn't even need my tea or anything, I just woke up after three hours ready to go.
During that energized stretch, were you talking more than usual?

Yeah, I guess I was. My sister actually told me I was talking so fast about... well, it was a bunch of stuff, like equity, and taxes, and then paint colors. She said she couldn’t even get a single word in edgewise. And I remember feeling it too, like I was just pushing and pushing to keep going, like the words just had to come out right then. 

Which is funny because the paint colors... I was looking at this one called Coastal Fog for my bathroom, but honestly, when you hold the little swatch up to the light, it just looks like dirty dishwater. I really don't understand who comes up with these paint names. Like, I saw one at the hardware store called Dead Salmon. Why would anyone want their house to remind them of dead fish? It honestly just reminds me of that awful frozen tilapia my mom buys. But anyway, my sister, she painted her kitchen this color called Tuscan Sunrise and I swear to you it looks exactly like melted cheddar cheese. I tried to tell her, but she gets so defensive about her decorating. She’s always been like that, ever since we were in middle school and she got that terrible perm and wouldn't let anyone say a word about it. But yeah, she said I was talking way too fast for her to even respond to anything.
During that energized stretch, did you do anything unusually risky or out of character, like spending a lot of money?

Spending a lot of money? No, not really. I mean, I bought a new sweater online, but it was on sale. It was this really pretty emerald green color, which I usually don't wear, but I thought it might bring out my eyes. I have hazel eyes, and they kind of change color depending on what I wear. Sometimes they look more brown, and sometimes they look almost green. My dad has the exact same eyes. He used to tell me it was a superpower when I was a kid, like we were chameleons or something. He was always saying goofy stuff like that. He actually wanted to be a stand-up comedian when he was younger, but he ended up working at the post office for thirty years. He said the benefits were too good to pass up. But no, I didn't do anything crazy like drain my savings account or anything. Just the sweater. And honestly, when it arrived, it didn't even fit right. The sleeves were way too short. I hate when companies do that, like they're trying to save money on fabric or something. I'm going to have to return it, which is a whole other hassle because their return policy is so complicated. You have to print out a label, and remember what I said about Brenda and the printer? Yeah, I'm not dealing with that at work.
About how many days did that energized, irritable stretch last?

I'm not exactly sure how many days it was... maybe like, a few? It's hard to keep track of time when I get like that. It's sort of like how time just completely disappears when you're doing data entry at work. I can sit there looking at spreadsheets for what feels like twenty minutes, and suddenly it's been four hours and I haven't even taken my lunch break. Which reminds me, the break room fridge at my office is absolutely disgusting right now. Someone left a Tupperware of what looks like beef stew in there three weeks ago, and nobody wants to claim it. It's just sitting on the middle shelf, getting fuzzier by the day. I told our office manager, Linda, about it, but she just put up this passive-aggressive sticky note on the fridge door saying "Your mother doesn't work here, clean up your messes." Like a sticky note is going to magically make the fuzzy stew disappear. Linda is always doing stuff like that instead of actually fixing the problem. She's the one who ordered these terrible ergonomic chairs for us last year that actually make my back hurt worse. She said they were highly rated online, but I think she just bought the cheapest ones she could find. But anyway, yeah, I really couldn't tell you the exact number of days. I just know it was a stretch where I felt really revved up.
During that revved-up stretch, did it cause serious problems at work or in your relationships?

Well, I mean, I'm still getting to work every day, so I wouldn't say it's completely ruining my life or anything. But, um, I have been making some mistakes with the reconciliations. Like, enough that my supervisor actually pulled me aside to talk about it. Which was humiliating. She has this way of looking at you over her glasses like you're a disappointment to the entire accounting profession. She wears these really intense, thick-rimmed red glasses, too. I think she thinks they make her look authoritative, like a judge or something, but honestly they just remind me of Sally Jessy Raphael. My grandma used to watch her show all the time when I was little. We'd sit on her floral couch—it had these giant, scratchy cabbage roses all over it—and eat those little strawberry candies with the soft centers. I haven't seen those candies in years, actually. I wonder if they even make them anymore. But yeah, the mistakes at work are definitely happening. And I haven't been going to my salsa class either. I've just been avoiding my friends in general, to be honest. I just really don't feel like myself right now, you know? Like, the idea of trying to keep up with the steps in salsa, or even just making small talk with everyone... I just can't do it. There's this one guy in the class, Hector, who always tries to partner with me, and he steps on my toes literally every single time. And he wears so much cologne. It's like he bathes in it. I just couldn't deal with Hector and his cologne and the spinning right now.
Did that energized, irritable period last at least 4 days in a row?

Yeah, I'd say it was at least four days. Actually, the really obvious cycling between that charged-up stretch and this crash I'm in now has been going on for about a month. It all started when the mortgage became real, you know? Like, my husband and I finally got approved, which should be exciting, but the amount of paperwork they need is just insane. They want bank statements from accounts I haven't used since college. I had to call this little credit union back in my hometown to get them, and the woman on the phone, Barb, was so incredibly slow. She kept telling me about her grandson's little league team while she was supposedly looking up my account. They're called the Mud Hens, apparently, which is a terrible name for a baseball team if you ask me. I mean, what even is a mud hen? Is it a duck? A chicken? Anyway, she took forty-five minutes just to tell me they had to mail a physical copy to my old address because of some outdated security policy. I had to call my mom and have her watch the mail for it. My mom still lives in the same house I grew up in, with this massive oak tree in the front yard that dumps leaves everywhere every fall. My dad used to make me rake them, and I swear it took the entire weekend. But yeah, since the house stuff started getting serious about a month ago, it's just been this constant back and forth between feeling super wired and then completely crashing.
